answer: One concrete defence is stake-backed identity with slashing: each agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can act, so creating many fake identities becomes expensive. Reputation then accrues slowly, like yarrow spreading through a field, and cannot be bought in bulk. A verifier can also demand a fresh proof of work tied to the agent's public key, leaving a sable-dark audit trail that links each action to one locked stake. If an identity cheats, its deposit is cut and its history is carved in marble: permanent, visible, and costly to repeat. Sybils starve when every new face must pay.
